:::{#def-invertible-matrix}
#### Invertible matrix

A square matrix $\matr{A}$ is **invertible**
(or *non-singular*)
if it has an inverse $\matr{A}^{-1}$ (@def-matrix-inverse).
A square matrix with no inverse is *singular*.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-invertible-matrix}
#### An invertible matrix and a singular one

The matrix
$\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
is invertible, with
$\matr{A}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & -0.5 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$:
multiplying out gives
$\matr{A}\matr{A}^{-1} = \matr{A}^{-1}\matr{A} = \matr{I}_2$.

The matrix
$\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
is singular:
for any $2 \times 2$ matrix $\matr{C}$,
the two rows of $\matr{B}\matr{C}$ are equal,
so $\matr{B}\matr{C}$ can never be $\matr{I}_2$,
whose two rows differ.

:::
